subject.title: San Francisco Public Defender

positions.statement: Mano Raju is running unopposed, and we're giving him a weak endorsement.

subject.title: San Francisco Board of Supervisors, District 2

positions.statement: Sherrill has done a great job as Supervisor, and we're excited to see him keep working alongside Mayor Lurie to get San Francisco back on track. That's why he has our endorsement.

subject.title: San Francisco Board of Supervisors, District 4

positions.statement: District 4 asked for a supervisor who listens, and in less than a year Wong has voted their priorities, delivered visible wins, and won their votes once already. That's why he has our endorsement.

subject.title: San Francisco Board of Supervisors, District 6

positions.statement: We recommend voting for Matt Dorsey for Supervisor, District 6.

subject.title: San Francisco Board of Supervisors, District 8

positions.statement: We recommend voting for Darshini Patel as your #1 choice for Supervisor, District 8.

subject.title: San Francisco Board of Supervisors, District 10

positions.statement: We recommend voting for Theo Ellington for Supervisor, District 10.

subject.title: San Francisco — Proposition A (Charter Changes Affecting Various City Departments and Commissions)

positions.statement: Departments will answer to elected individuals, not unelected commissioners, so voters can actually hold them accountable. Every link in the chain of command will now end with you. Vote yes on Prop A.

subject.title: San Francisco — Proposition B (Establishing a Municipal Finance Corporation and a Public Bank)

positions.statement: Let's at least get our own finances in order before trying to run a bank. Vote no on Prop B.

subject.title: San Francisco — Proposition C (Contributions to the Housing Fund)

positions.statement: We support real money for subsidized housing. That's why we endorsed Prop C, which grows the Housing Trust Fund to $125M per year and lets the Board pause contributions in bad budget years.

subject.title: San Francisco — Proposition D (Changes to Ballot Measure Process)

positions.statement: Vote yes on Prop D to shorten your ballot.

subject.title: San Francisco — Proposition E (City Administrator's Authority and Changes to City Contracting)

positions.statement: Vote yes on Prop E.

subject.title: San Francisco — Proposition F (Changes to Executive Branch Management)

positions.statement: Vote yes on Prop F.

subject.title: San Francisco — Proposition G (Allowing Private Vehicles on the Great Highway in Sunset Dunes Park)

positions.statement: Vote no on Prop G. Let's all move on.

subject.title: San Francisco — Proposition H (Parcel Tax to Fund Public Muni Operations)

positions.statement: Vote yes on Prop H.

subject.title: San Francisco — Proposition I (Changes to Real Property Transfer Tax)

positions.statement: Vote no on Prop I.

subject.title: San Francisco — Proposition J (Removal of Foreclosure Exemption for Real Property Transfer Tax)

positions.statement: For that deal to happen, Prop J must pass and Prop I must fail, because Prop I would take away the Board's power to change the tax.

subject.title: Bay Area — Regional Measure RTM (Regional Transit Measure)

positions.statement: The economy of the entire Bay Area depends on keeping transit running. Vote yes on the Regional Transit Measure.

subject.title: Governor of California

positions.statement: Preliminary endorsement — Xavier Becerra has not returned our questionnaire. We recommend voting for Xavier Becerra for Governor.

subject.title: Lieutenant Governor of California

positions.statement: In June we endorsed Josh Fryday, who unfortunately finished third and didn't advance. The general election is now Fiona Ma, a Democrat, against Gloria Romero, a Republican, and Ma is the clear choice.

subject.title: California Secretary of State

positions.statement: Preliminary endorsement — Shirley Weber has not returned our questionnaire. Shirley Weber has done the job competently, and we endorse her for another term.

subject.title: California Controller

positions.statement: We recommend voting for Malia Cohen for State Controller.

subject.title: California Treasurer

positions.statement: Kounalakis is the only candidate in this race with private-sector experience doing exactly that. That's why she has our endorsement.

subject.title: Attorney General of California

positions.statement: Rob Bonta has been an effective Attorney General, and we're happy to endorse him for another term.

subject.title: California Insurance Commissioner

positions.statement: We strongly recommend Ben Allen and strongly oppose Jane Kim.

subject.title: California State Board of Equalization, District 2

positions.statement: We endorsed Sally Lieber in the June primary, but we've decided to change our endorsement to John Pimentel for the general election.

subject.title: California Superintendent of Public Instruction

positions.statement: We recommend voting for Richard Barrera for State Superintendent of Public Instruction.

subject.title: California — Proposition 1 (Authorizes Bonds for Housing Affordability Programs)

positions.statement: Vote Yes on Prop 1 to build the homes California has already approved.

subject.title: California — Proposition 2 (Increases State's Rainy Day Fund)

positions.statement: Reasonable people can disagree about the right amount to save, and whether the government should be forced to do so, so consider this endorsement a weak yes.

subject.title: California — Proposition 3 (Provides Permanent Funding for Schools and Health Care by Extending Existing Tax on High Incomes)

positions.statement: We think voters should make these tax rates permanent and vote yes.

subject.title: California — Proposition 4 (Repeals Prohibition Against Public Funding of Election Campaigns)

positions.statement: Public financing in San Francisco has meant donors give less, taxpayers pay more, and elections come out the same. Vote no on Prop 4.

subject.title: California — Proposition 5 (Changes Recall Election Process for Statewide Officers)

positions.statement: This is an easy fix and an easy yes.

subject.title: California — Proposition 37 (Creates Loan Program for Middle-Income Buyers of Qualified New Homes)

positions.statement: Let's give it a shot and see if it works.

subject.title: California — Proposition 38 (Authorizes Bonds for Immunology Medical Research)

positions.statement: Research is a good cause and it's great that the state and federal government fund it, and that is exactly why it deserves better than a bond one donor wrote around his own institute. Vote no.

subject.title: California — Proposition 39 (Prohibits Citizens from Voting Unless They Present Government-Issued Identification)

positions.statement: all to chase a non-existent problem, all while making your own ballot easier to reject. Vote no.

subject.title: California — Proposition 40 (Imposes One-Time Tax on Certain Taxpayers)

positions.statement: Fund health care with money that shows up. Vote no on Prop 40, and yes on Prop 3.

subject.title: California — Proposition 41 (Prohibits New State Taxes That Exclude Revenues from State Spending Limit. Requires Audits for New State Special Taxes)

positions.statement: Constitutional limits bind until voters change them. Fix the Gann limit; don't evade it. Vote yes.

subject.title: California — Proposition 42 (Prohibits New State Personal Property Taxes and Certain Retroactive State Taxes)

positions.statement: Prop 42 keeps every tax California has and stops only the ones that tax you for owning what you already earned. Vote yes.

subject.title: California — Proposition 43 (Limits Voters' Ability to Raise Revenues for Local Government Services)

positions.statement: Vote yes on Prop 43.

subject.title: California — Proposition 44 (Requires Community Health Clinics Spend 90% Of Revenue on Program Services)

positions.statement: A labor dispute belongs at the bargaining table. Don't let it be settled by fining the clinics your neighbors depend on. Vote no.

subject.title: California — Proposition 45 (Modifies Environmental Review for Certain Projects)

positions.statement: Delay is a policy choice, and you pay for it in rent, energy bills, and water rates. Vote yes.

subject.title: US House of Representatives, California District 11

positions.statement: Scott Wiener has shown he can pass hard laws on the issues San Francisco most needs solved. Connie Chan has spent her career blocking; Wiener has spent his delivering. That's why he has our endorsement.

subject.title: US House of Representatives, California District 15

positions.statement: Preliminary endorsement — Kevin Mullin has not returned our questionnaire. We recommend voting for Kevin Mullin for House of Representatives, District 15.
